beats.t: At the end of their descent along the threads lay a red sky. Beneath it, stone temples stretched endlessly. A little moon floated above every roof.
Why are there so many moons?
Twenty-seven. Here the Moon spends one night in each house, staying twenty-seven nights.
The Moon uses guesthouses? Who pays for the rooms?
That's a new question for me. I'll write it down.
Red threads hung along both sides of the stone steps, stretching from pillar to pillar, roof to sky. Whenever the wind blew, they hummed low.
These threads look like the ones in the twelfth house.
The same thread. There it showed the end; here it shows the link between lives.
A sky that reads bonds. Twenty-seven houses where the Moon stays.
So this is the sky for love readings.
More precisely, karma, bonds, and romance. All three are expensive.
A stone tablet stood at the temple entrance. Instead of words, it bore pictures: a serpent with only a head, and a serpent with only a tail.
The head and tail are separate. They look like they used to be one creature.
A tale of a beheaded serpent. Three days to hear it all.
Three lines.
A serpent stole the drink of immortality and was beheaded. Rahu, the head, swallows the sun, while Ketu, the tail…
Yundal stopped and looked at the tail carved on the slab.
The tail does what?
I think we'll see for ourselves soon.
Couldn't even fill three lines.
An enemy faster than its explanation.
At that moment, one moon darkened. It was staying in a house rounded like an ox's forehead. A black shadow passed slowly before it.
Rohini, the Moon's place toward Taurus. You can see the head there.
Black Moon?
Rahu, the head, sits in Rohini. Ketu, the tail, is opposite in Jyeshtha.
Stop trespassing in other people's skies!
Let's charge ten times the late fees. We learned that from Blue Rabbit.
Neo sat alone beside a stone well, his outer coat covering his right arm.
Yeoni touched an underlined note: Neo's hand. Must see it later. There could be no more later.
It's later now.
...You're still carrying that note?
Never threw it away. Give me your arm.
Neo slowly lifted his coat. His arm was empty above the elbow. Blue light from the well passed through it and pooled on the ground.
How far will it go? Your legs? Your whole body?
I'm repaying a borrowed place. Once it's repaid, it will end.
If you keep saying repayment without telling me what you borrowed, how am I supposed to help?
You don't need to. If you know, the price goes up.
Yeoni wrapped both hands around his transparent arm. She caught nothing. Still, she didn't let go.
Then I'll hold it without knowing. That doesn't raise the price, does it?
...That wasn't in the calculation.
The wind stopped, and the well water stilled. Color briefly returned to the reflected hand. Yeoni hurried to draw its outline in the notebook, leaving out none of its five fingers.
Moka, tell me your birthday and I'll read your lunar station. Free.
'Free' is the most suspicious word you say.
Then shall I guess? Quick hands, angry at compliments, always making sure others eat first.
...You just described what you've seen me do.
Half of divination is observation. The other half is courage.
Moka's face is red.
I've spent too long near the fire! Occupational hazard of being a chef!
Then a temple bell rang once. One moon moved from its roof to the next, signaling that a night had passed.
Time moves quickly here. Every time the Moon moves house, a day passes.
We've already used up a day?
We should hurry. Delay is expensive in this sky.
If time's so precious, why were you all talking about my face?
In a round chamber deep in the temple, twenty-seven spaces circled the floor. An unlit lamp stood in each.
Only your own fire lights your Moon's place. The house where the Moon stayed on your birth night.
She gathered a small, steady flame at her fingertips. The first lamp only singed and went out. The second accepted the fire and burned without flickering.
Bharani. The star that bears.
Bears?
A star that holds life, then brings it into the world. In this sky, such people are called vessels.
Yeoni instinctively pressed their stomach. That was Black Moon's word. Cold. Hungry.
I hate that word. Vessel. That's what Black Moon calls me.
Black Moon told only half of it. Empty to be filled—that's his meaning.
Bharani doesn't hoard. It holds, nurtures, and gives back.
Yeoni took her hand from her belly, then laid it there again. A little less afraid than before.
When she touched fire to the third space, Krittika's lamp surged blade-white. She stepped back, almost burning her hand.
My Moon is right beside that?
Only near the boundary. You choose which way to lean.
Then the nurturing side. I've just chosen.
Yundal. Can you read Seo Hanbi's star too?
Not without her birthday. Do you know it?
The parcel label only had her name and apartment number. No birthday.
Then we'll have to ask her directly. Though I don't know whether she'll answer.
A single red thread descended from the round room's ceiling and wrapped around Yeoni's wrist. It wasn't cold. It was lukewarm, like skin.
Why is this wrapping around me?
Your thread of connection. Follow it to the end and you'll find the person you're linked to.
Wow. Time to reveal your destined partner? The cat must be nervous.
I am not nervous.
The thread split in two. One strand led to Neo, the other beneath a crack in the temple floor.
Yeoni's expression froze as they followed the thread toward Neo. Just before it reached his chest, it had unraveled. Only a few fibers kept it connected.
Neo. What's wrong with this? It's frayed.
It's an old thread. That's normal.
What do you mean, always like that? Your arm, the thread—are you going to say it about everything?
Neo covered the thread with his hand. The fibers, close to snapping, remained visible through his transparent palm. He couldn't hide them.
My lady. The other strand. That one goes down.
(Down. Where the chains were dragged.)
Yeoni tugged gently. From below came the faintest answering pull, as though someone held the other end between their fingers.
You can hold only one branch of a split thread. Hold both, and your Moon wears away instead.
Instead of answering, she seized Neo's thread with her other hand too.
Bharani's lamp shuddered. The flame halved, and half its wick burned black.
Let go of mine. That thread was always like that.
No. Frayed things can be stitched.
She wound each thread once around her wrist. The lamp stayed half-dim and never grew again.
Yeoni reached toward the lamp, then stopped. Opening the hands that held both threads might lose the pull from below. Instead, she fixed the remaining wick's length in her mind.
I'll check that flame first when we return. If it's smaller, we'll know something happened while we were down there.
The downward thread wasn't made in a single life. It's thick enough to survive many rebirths.
Then that person below and I met in another life too?
And exchanged something, likely. Good or bad.
What if it was bad?
Then I have even more questions.
The temple floor split open. The end of an enormous tail rose through the gap, covered in serpent scales. Chains coiled tightly around it.
The tail eats yesterday; the head, tomorrow. Which wilt thou offer first, vessel?
Neither! Our Yeoni isn't hungry!
I'll take it into the Void. Everyone back.
As Yundal reached for his glove, Neo pressed down on his wrist. His hand was transparent, but its grip still held.
Don't widen it yet. We can't spend everything before the head arrives.
Mr. Cat worrying about me. I'm touched.
The tail swept the floor. Lamps toppled; only half-burned Bharani held firm. The red thread tightened on her wrist. Someone held its lower end.
Rain sounded from beneath the crack, impossible in the clear temple. Then came a low, elegant voice.
Don't let go of that thread. Not yet.
The tail sank back into the gap. The floor closed. Only the thread remained around Yeoni's wrist, stretched straight and tight downward.
I know that voice.
Yeoni.
Don't stop me. I said I had a mountain of questions. I'm going down to ask them.
I'm not stopping you. I said I'd stand beside you.
I'm coming too. Giving people a hard time is my specialty.
I'll applaud from behind the people asking questions. Applause is free.
The four headed for the temple's deepest stairs. The steps led into darkness. The red thread around Yeoni's wrist guided them onward.
Twenty-seven moons shone in sequence along the stairwell wall. As they descended, the moons went out one by one. When only the last remained, the rain sounded very close.
